title: PASTURE AND RANGE MANAGEMENT
mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is made up of grasses, forbs, legumes, sedges, vines, and shrubs."
The understory is made up of grasses, forbs, legumes, sedges, vines, and shrubs.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the dominant world producer of lupins, accounting for around 85% of world production."
Lupins Australia is the dominant world producer of lupins, accounting for around 85% of world production.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are the same as if the over story was closed."
The effects are the same as if the over story was closed.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a large country with varying vegetation belts."
Nigeria is a large country with varying vegetation belts.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a short-term management tool since its effect is usually immediate and does not last more than one grazing cycle."
Fertilizing with nitrogen is a short-term management tool since its effect is usually immediate and does not last more than one grazing cycle.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an oilseed containing about 20 percent oil."
Soyabean is an oilseed containing about 20 percent oil.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a measure of the proportion of grass that can be utilized by an animal."
Digestibility is a measure of the proportion of grass that can be utilized by an animal.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the most commonly-used method for estimating forage yield."
Using a grazing stick is the most commonly-used method for estimating forage yield.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is a common warm- season grass but it is too tall for a pasture."
Corn is a common warm- season grass but it is too tall for a pasture.

Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the final product when forage of sufficient moisture (> ~50%) is conserved and stored anaerobically (oxygen-free), under conditions that encourage fermentation of sugars to organic acids."
Silage is the final product when forage of sufficient moisture (> ~50%) is conserved and stored anaerobically (oxygen-free), under conditions that encourage fermentation of sugars to organic acids.
